Q1: Which commit must have a successful `CI / lint` check-run before the release job tags?
Choices:
A) The tested source commit (`RELEASE_TESTED_SHA` in `test-and-mark-stable.yml`, the checked-out source SHA in `mark-stable.yml`). The tagged commit may only add the changelog-assembly commit on top, and that is enforced: its parent must be the tested commit and it may change only `CHANGELOG.md` and `changelog.d/`. (RECOMMENDED)
B) The commit that actually gets tagged. The job pushes the changelog commit, waits a bounded time for CI on it, and only then tags. This is slower, and the push to `stable` can start other workflows first.
C) Both: the tested commit must pass before the changelog commit is made, and the tagged commit must pass before the stable tag moves.
Q2: When `STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED` is unset or not `true` (the default), what should a release-workflow run do?
Choices:
A) Run all validation as usual, including the new CI check, but skip the tagging/release step, the consumer dispatch and the sync-to-main step. Log a `::notice::` naming the flag. The run ends green, so `auto-release-stable.yml` doesn't keep retrying the same tip. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Same as A, but the run ends in failure so operators see a red run. Note: every scheduled `auto-release-stable` and promote-cycle run then counts as a failed attempt and uses up its retry budget.
C) Exit straight away without running validation.
